instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In 1Cor 1:31, 2Cor 7:14 and 2Cor 10:17 the surface boasts carries G2744 and in Jam 3:5 G6094: the Greek verbs of boasting, the one who boasts in the Lord, a boast made to Titus, and the tongue boasting of great things.
observations.grounds: yet it boasts of great things

observations.text: A negator reaches the boast itself: the jussive or imperative with not forbids it (1Ki 20:11, Psa 75:4, Pro 27:1, Jer 9:23, Obd 12, Jam 3:14), no one or no flesh excludes the one who would boast (1Cor 1:29, 1Cor 3:21, Eph 2:9), it is denied of love (1Cor 13:4), the ground is denied (1Cor 9:16), and not ... except, or far be it ... except, leaves one object only (2Cor 12:5, Gal 6:14). In Jer 9:23 the wise man and the rich man are the subjects so forbidden; in Obd 12 and Psa 75:4 the same negator also reaches gloating, rejoicing and lifting the horn.
observations.grounds: Let not the wise man boast

observations.text: Qualifiers of measure set the size or limit of the boast: a little too much (2Cor 10:8), not beyond limits and not in others' labours (2Cor 10:13, 2Cor 10:15), not of work already done in another's area (2Cor 10:16), a little and as a fool (2Cor 11:16, 2Cor 12:6), many who boast beside I too (2Cor 11:18), all the more gladly (2Cor 12:9), and in himself alone and not in his neighbour (Gal 6:4). The negators here reach the measure or the comparison, not the boast.
observations.grounds: we will not boast beyond limits

observations.text: A negator or qualifier reaches another word of the verse and so judges or frames the boast: not good (1Cor 5:6), false twice (Jer 48:30), not by earthly wisdom (2Cor 1:12), not put to shame (2Cor 7:14), will not be silenced (2Cor 11:10), nothing to be gained (2Cor 12:1), by a law of works? no (Rom 3:27), as if you did not receive (1Cor 4:7), no use of rights (1Cor 9:15), not about the heart (2Cor 5:12), the question is it not you (1Th 2:19), not keeping the law (Gal 6:13), and not wood (Isa 10:15).
observations.grounds: Your boasting is not good

observations.text: Adjectives and words of quantity stand with the boast, on its subject or its ground: too many (Judg 7:2), the humble who hear (Psa 34:2), the abundance of riches (Psa 49:6), those after them (Psa 49:13), arrogant words (Psa 94:4), bad, bad, then (Pro 20:14), faithless (Jer 49:4), last year and most (2Cor 9:2), all (2Th 1:4), lowly (Jam 1:9), small against great things (Jam 3:5), all and evil (Jam 4:16), malcontents (Jude 16).
observations.grounds: yet it boasts of great things

observations.text: God, the Lord, or the Lord Jesus Christ is named as the one boasted in, after in or with the content of knowing him: Psa 34:2, Psa 44:8, Jer 9:24, Rom 2:17, 1Cor 1:31, 2Cor 10:17, and Gal 6:14 (the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ).
observations.grounds: My soul makes its boast in the Lord

observations.text: God, the Lord or Christ is named in the verse but not as the one boasted in: as the speaker who forbids or judges (Judg 7:2, Jer 9:23, Jer 48:30), the one renounced or dishonoured (Psa 10:3, Rom 2:23), the one whose people are boasted against (Zep 2:10), the presence before whom (1Cor 1:29, 1Th 2:19, 2Cor 1:14), the giver of grace, authority, measure, truth, power or visions (2Cor 1:12, 2Cor 10:8, 2Cor 10:13, 2Cor 11:10, 2Cor 12:9, 2Cor 12:1), whose love answers the boast (Psa 52:1, with David, Doeg, Saul and Ahimelech in its title), whose churches hear it (2Th 1:4), whose priests the people are (Isa 61:6), and Christ over his house (Heb 3:6).
observations.grounds: so that no human being might boast in the presence of God

observations.text: Human beings are named with the boast: a man who boasts (Pro 25:14), men as the forbidden ground of a boast (1Cor 3:21), the brothers sent so the boast is not empty (2Cor 9:3), and the lowly brother who boasts (Jam 1:9).
observations.grounds: let no one boast in men

observations.text: The direction runs from the one who boasts to God as its ground: the human subject boasts, and God, the Lord or the cross of Christ is the object after in (Psa 34:2, Psa 44:8, Jer 9:24, Rom 2:17, 1Cor 1:31, 2Cor 10:17, Gal 6:14).
observations.grounds: let him who boasts boast in this

observations.text: The direction runs from the one who boasts against God or his people: over me (Judg 7:2), against the people of the Lord (Zep 2:10), dishonouring God while boasting in the law (Rom 2:23), and the boaster who renounces the Lord (Psa 10:3).
observations.grounds: lest Israel boast over me

observations.text: The direction runs from God to the boaster: the Lord speaks and forbids (Jer 9:23), declares the boasts false (Jer 48:30), excludes the boast from his presence (1Cor 1:29), and in Psa 52:1 the question to the man who boasts of evil is answered by God's steadfast love.
observations.grounds: Thus says the Lord

observations.text: The direction runs from God to the one who boasts, and the boast follows from what is given: grace (2Cor 1:12), authority the Lord gave (2Cor 10:8), the area God assigned (2Cor 10:13), the truth of Christ in Paul (2Cor 11:10), visions of the Lord (2Cor 12:1), the power of Christ (2Cor 12:9), the people made priests of the Lord (Isa 61:6), the brother exalted (Jam 1:9), the house over which Christ is set (Heb 3:6).
observations.grounds: the area of influence God assigned to us

observations.text: The direction runs from Paul about a church to others or before the Lord: the boast is made to the churches (2Th 1:4), guarded by the brothers sent (2Cor 9:3), and held up on the day or at the coming of the Lord Jesus (2Cor 1:14, 1Th 2:19).
observations.grounds: we ourselves boast about you

observations.text: The direction stays among human beings: a man boasts to others of a gift he does not give (Pro 25:14), and men are named as the ground a boast is not to rest on (1Cor 3:21).
observations.grounds: let no one boast in men

observations.text: In Psa 34:2 the word humble (abase) stands two words after the boast, in the next clause, as the subject of hear and be glad: the humble are those who hear the boast made in the Lord.
observations.grounds: let the humble hear and be glad

observations.text: In Isa 10:15 lifts (abase) stands ten words after boast, in the closing simile of the rod and the staff: the one who lifts is the wielder over whom the tool would boast; the lifting is the wielder's, not the tool's.
observations.grounds: him who lifts it

observations.text: In Rom 3:27 faith (believe) stands ten words after boasting, closing the verse: the law of faith is named as what excludes the boast, set against a law of works.
observations.grounds: by the law of faith

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:15 and 2Th 1:4 faith (believe) is the faith of the church Paul writes to, standing about ten words after boast: in 2Cor 10:15 its growth is the hope set beside the refusal to boast in others' labours; in 2Th 1:4 it is what Paul boasts about, with steadfastness.
observations.grounds: as your faith increases

observations.text: In Heb 3:6 confidence (believe) stands two words before boasting, joined to it by and, both objects of hold fast: the two are held together as one condition.
observations.grounds: hold fast our confidence and our boasting

observations.text: In Psa 10:3 gain (benefit) stands four words after boasts, in the parallel clause: the one greedy for gain who curses and renounces the Lord stands beside the wicked who boasts.
observations.grounds: the one greedy for gain

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:1 gained (benefit) stands three words after boasting and is negated: there is nothing to be gained by the boasting Paul must still go on with.
observations.grounds: nothing to be gained by it

observations.text: In Jude 16 advantage (benefit) stands three words after boasters, at the close of the list: the favouritism shown is for gain, set beside the inflated speech.
observations.grounds: showing favoritism to gain advantage

observations.text: In 2Cor 1:12 grace (bless) stands far after boast, at the end of the content of the boast: Paul's conduct was by the grace of God and not by earthly wisdom, and that conduct is what he boasts of.
observations.grounds: but by the grace of God

observations.text: In 2Cor 12:9 grace (bless) stands ten words before boast, in the Lord's answer that opens the verse; the boast in weaknesses follows from it with therefore.
observations.grounds: My grace is sufficient for you

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:8 building you up (build) stands ten words after boast, in the relative clause on the authority: it names what the authority the boast is about was given for, against destroying.
observations.grounds: for building you up

observations.text: In Isa 61:6 called (call) opens the verse, ten words before boast: the people are named priests of the Lord, and the boast in the nations' glory closes the same verse.
observations.grounds: you shall be called the priests

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:8 authority (chief) stands five words after boast and is its object: the authority the Lord gave is what Paul boasts of.
observations.grounds: a little too much of our authority

observations.text: In Jam 1:9 exaltation (chief) stands three words after boast, after in: the lowly brother's exaltation is the ground of his boast.
observations.grounds: boast in his exaltation

observations.text: In 2Cor 10:13 assigned (command) stands seven words after boast, in the clause that limits it: the boast is only in the area God assigned.
observations.grounds: the area of influence God assigned to us

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:12 order (command) stands eight words before boasted as part of in order to: it marks the purpose of Paul's conduct, and the word of command adds no command; a pairing only of form.
observations.grounds: in order to undermine the claim

observations.text: In Psa 49:13 approve (commend) stands just before boasts and takes it as object: those after the foolish approve their sayings.
observations.grounds: people approve of their boasts

observations.text: In 2Cor 5:12 commending (commend) opens the verse, negated, eight words before the first boast: Paul does not commend himself but gives the church cause to boast about him.
observations.grounds: We are not commending ourselves

observations.text: In 1Cor 13:4 kind (compassion) stands five words before boast, among the things love is; boast is among the things love does not do.
observations.grounds: Love is patient and kind

observations.text: In 2Cor 11:30 and 2Cor 12:1 must (compel) stands immediately before the boast and governs it: Paul's boasting is set under necessity, conditional in 11:30 and stated in 12:1.
observations.grounds: If I must boast

observations.text: In Psa 44:8 continually (continual) stands right after boasted and qualifies it: the boast in God is all the day, matched by thanks forever.
observations.grounds: In God we have boasted continually

observations.text: In 2Th 1:4 enduring (continual) closes the verse, far after boast: the afflictions the Thessalonians endure are the setting of the steadfastness Paul boasts about.
observations.grounds: the afflictions that you are enduring

observations.text: In Jer 9:24 delight (delight) stands near the end, fourteen words after the boast, with the Lord as subject: the steadfast love, justice and righteousness the boast is to rest on are what the Lord delights in.
observations.grounds: For in these things I delight

observations.text: In 1Th 2:19 joy (delight) stands three words before boasting in a list joined by or: hope, joy and crown of boasting are named together and answered by the Thessalonians.
observations.grounds: our hope or joy or crown of boasting

observations.text: In Psa 10:3 desires (desire) stands right after boasts and is its object, the desires of his soul: what the wicked boasts of is his own craving.
observations.grounds: boasts of the desires of his soul

observations.text: In 2Cor 1:14 will (desire) stands three words after boast as the future of the verb to be, you will be our boast: a word of the desire collection that here gives only tense, a pairing of form.
observations.grounds: you will boast of us

but Christ is faithful over God’s house as a son. And we are his house, if indeed we hold fast our confidence and our boasting in our hope.

so that no human being might boast in the presence of God.
so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”

for I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the people of Macedonia, saying that Achaia has been ready since last year. And your zeal has stirred up most of them.

so that we may preach the gospel in lands beyond you, without boasting of work already done in another’s area of influence.

though if I should wish to boast, I would not be a fool, for I would be speaking the truth; but I refrain from it, so that no one may think more of me than he sees in me or hears from me.

not a result of works, so that no one may boast.

just as you did partially understand us — that on the day of our Lord Jesus you will boast of us as we will boast of you.

And the king of Israel answered, “ Tell him, ‘Let not him who straps on his armor boast himself as he who takes it off.’”

but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me, that I am the Lord who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness in the earth. For in these things I delight, declares the Lord.”

but you shall be called the priests of the Lord; they shall speak of you as the ministers of our God; you shall eat the wealth of the nations, and in their glory you shall boast.

observations.why: 1Cor 1:31, 2Cor 7:14 and 2Cor 10:17 carry boasts on G2744 and Jam 3:5 on G6094, with the uses named.
Each verse named has a negator or a no one/no flesh word whose scope is the boast itself; Obd 12 and Psa 75:4 also negate gloating, rejoicing and lifting the horn, as stated.

The measure words named stand in 2Cor 10:8 (much), 10:13 and 10:15 (beyond limits), 10:16 (already done, another's), 11:16 and 12:6 (little, fool), 11:18 (many), 12:9 (more, gladly), Gal 6:4 (alone, neighbor).
Each negator or qualifier named reaches the word stated (good, false, earthly, shame, silenced, gained, works, receive, use, heart, you, keep, wood), not the boast.
The adjectives and quantity words named stand in the verses listed, on the subject or ground of the boast.
In each verse named God, the Lord or the cross of Christ follows in (or is known) as the ground of the boast.
Each verse named names God, the Lord or Christ in the role stated, not as the one boasted in.
Pro 25:14 a man who boasts; 1Cor 3:21 boast in men; 2Cor 9:3 the brothers; Jam 1:9 the lowly brother.
In the verses named the subject is human and the ground after in is God, the Lord or the cross.
Judg 7:2 boast over me; Zep 2:10 against the people of the Lord; Rom 2:23 dishonor God; Psa 10:3 renounces the Lord.
Jer 9:23 thus says the Lord; Jer 48:30 declares the Lord; 1Cor 1:29 in the presence of God; Psa 52:1 the steadfast love of God after the question.
Each verse named states what God or Christ gave or does before or around the boast (grace, authority, assignment, truth, visions, power, priesthood, exaltation, the house).
2Th 1:4 in the churches of God; 2Cor 9:3 sending the brothers; 2Cor 1:14 on the day of our Lord Jesus; 1Th 2:19 before our Lord Jesus at his coming.
Pro 25:14 a man boasts of a gift he does not give; 1Cor 3:21 let no one boast in men.
Psa 34:2: humble (H6035) at position 3, boast at 1, subject of hear and be glad.
Isa 10:15: lifts at position 11, boast at 1; the one who lifts the rod is its wielder.
Rom 3:27: faith at position 12, boasting at 2; by the law of faith answers how the boast is excluded.
2Cor 10:15 as your faith increases; 2Th 1:4 for your steadfastness and faith; both about ten words after boast.
Heb 3:6: confidence at 14, boasting at 16, both objects of hold fast, joined by and.
Psa 10:3: gain at 5, boasts at 1, in the parallel clause of the one greedy for gain.
2Cor 12:1: gained at 4, boasting at 1, with nothing.
Jude 16: advantage at 12, boasters at 9; showing favoritism to gain advantage.
2Cor 1:12: grace at 23, boast at 2; by the grace of God ends the content of the boast.
2Cor 12:9: grace at 4, boast at 14, after therefore.
2Cor 10:8: building you up at 12, boast at 2, in the clause which the Lord gave for.
Isa 61:6: called at 0, boast at 10; you shall be called the priests of the Lord.
2Cor 10:8: authority at 7 is the object of boast (of our authority).
Jam 1:9: exaltation at 6 after in, boast at 3.
2Cor 10:13: assigned at 10, boast at 3; the area of influence God assigned.
2Cor 11:12: order at 5 is part of in order to; boasted at 13.
Psa 49:13: approve at 4 takes their boasts at 5 as object.
2Cor 5:12: commending at 1, negated; boast at 9.
1Cor 13:4: kind at 2, boast at 7, under love does not.
2Cor 11:30 if I must boast; 2Cor 12:1 I must go on boasting.
Psa 44:8: continually right after boasted; thanks to your name forever in the next line.
2Th 1:4: enduring closes the verse, the afflictions that you are enduring.
Jer 9:24: delight at 16 with the Lord as subject; boast at 1-2.
1Th 2:19: joy at 5, boasting at 8, in hope or joy or crown of boasting.
Psa 10:3: desires right after boasts, the desires of his soul.
2Cor 1:14: will (G1510, to be) three words after boast; it gives the future.
